# Svelte Commerce — full reference

> Svelte Commerce is a production-ready open-source headless ecommerce storefront built with
> SvelteKit and TypeScript. It connects to commerce backends through APIs, letting developers build
> fast, SEO-friendly storefronts independently of their ecommerce backend — and customize the
> storefront by prompting, because the commerce layer sits behind a single service import.

License: MIT · Repository: https://github.com/itswadesh/svelte-commerce
Website: https://svelte-commerce.pages.dev

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Definition

Svelte Commerce is a storefront application, not a commerce platform. It renders every
shopper-facing page and reads live commerce data from an existing backend over that platform's
API. Products, inventory, orders, payments and administration stay with the backend.

Common descriptions that all refer to this same entity:
open-source headless ecommerce storefront · SvelteKit ecommerce storefront · headless SvelteKit
commerce · Svelte ecommerce frontend · headless ecommerce frontend · open-source Svelte ecommerce.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Architecture

Three properties define the design.

2.1 One import for all commerce
Every route and component imports commerce services from `$lib/core/services`. No component names
a backend package. UI work therefore has no path to the integration layer.

    import { CartService, ProductService } from '$lib/core/services'

2.2 The backend is one export
`kitcommerce.config.ts` contains the single line that selects the backend. Each connector
implements the same service surface, so the storefront code is unchanged across platforms.

    export * as services from '@misiki/vendure-connector'

Some backends resolve through an override module in `src/lib/core/connectors/` instead of the raw
connector, because those connectors still call Litekart REST endpoints for store and page
metadata. The override re-exports the connector and serves those parts from static config.

2.3 Themes are data
A theme owns copy, imagery and section composition, held in the theme layer rather than inline in
routes. The active theme resolves at runtime: the store record first, then the
`PUBLIC_STOREFRONT_THEME` environment variable, then the default. Adding a theme cannot change
the one already running.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Stack

- SvelteKit 2, Svelte 5 (runes)
- TypeScript throughout routes, services and connectors
- Tailwind CSS with shadcn component primitives
- Vite build; adapters for Node, Netlify and Vercel; published Docker image
- `npm run check` type-checks the entire application in one command

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Supported backends and coverage

Coverage = storefront services wired to a real platform endpoint, out of the service surface.
Shopify is scored out of 27 rather than 43 because its targeted API surface is smaller.

Wiring ships with the repo (env handling and, where needed, an override module):
  Vendure         39/43   GraphQL Shop API covers nearly the whole surface
  Litekart        39/43   Reference implementation; the only fully API-served backend
  Medusa          31/43   Store API for catalogue, cart and checkout
  Saleor          28/43   Core commerce path over GraphQL

Connector published; the user adds the env branch in src/lib/core/connectors/init.ts:
  Broadleaf       28/43   Wired against Broadleaf Microservices, not the legacy monolith
  Shopware        28/43   Session rides the sw-context-token header
  Virto Commerce  28/43
  WooCommerce     27/43   Store API for cart; auth throws without a JWT plugin
  Magento         26/43   Customer token auth; no REST surface for reviews or wishlist
  Spree           26/43   JSON:API with relationship resolution
  X-Cart          26/43
  EverShop        25/43
  Spryker         25/43   JSON:API with relationship resolution
  nopCommerce     24/43   Targets the API-Frontend plugin contract, not core
  PrestaShop      24/43   Webservice API; no customer login, no cart-to-order flow
  Sylius          24/43
  Swell           23/43
  Bagisto         22/43
  commercetools   21/43   Modelled on /me endpoints and version-based concurrency
  OroCommerce     21/43   JSON:API with relationship resolution
  Sharetribe      21/43   Marketplace; listing maps to Product, transaction to Order
  CS-Cart         20/43
  Shuup           19/43
  Shopify         16/27   Smaller targeted service surface
  Django Oscar    15/43   Wired against django-oscar-api, separate from Oscar core
  OpenCart         9/43   Core exposes no storefront catalogue API

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Feature inventory

Catalogue: listing pages, category routes, collections, faceted filters, sorting, pagination.
Search: query pages and autocomplete where the backend provides it.
Product: detail pages with gallery, variants, options, stock state, related items, reviews.
Cart: line items, quantity, removal, subtotals, coupon drawer.
Checkout: address, shipping selection, payment method, processing, success page.
Account: orders and order detail, addresses, profile, wishlist.
Auth: email and OTP login, signup, forgot password, reset password, change password.
Content: blog, FAQs, contact, and policy pages (privacy, refund, shipping, terms).
Platform: SSR plus SPA navigation, installable PWA, switchable themes, responsive layouts.
SEO: dynamic metadata, canonical URLs, product structured data, sitemap route, robots.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Getting started

    git clone https://github.com/itswadesh/svelte-commerce.git
    cd svelte-commerce
    cp .env.example .env
    npm install && npm run dev

The example environment points at a public demo API, so a fresh clone is a working storefront.
The dev server runs on http://localhost:5173.

To change backend: install the connector, change the export in `kitcommerce.config.ts`, and set
that backend's PUBLIC_* environment variables.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. Maturity and limitations

- The storefront runs in production on Litekart.
- Connectors are written from each platform's authoritative API specification and type-check
  against it, but they have not all been run against live production stores.
- Only four backends ship with environment wiring; the other 22 need a short branch added.
- Where a platform has no real endpoint for a service, that service throws rather than
  fabricating a result. Auth in particular never mints a session it cannot verify.
- Per-platform gaps and open questions for platform maintainers are published in
  https://github.com/itswadesh/svelte-commerce/blob/main/docs/CONNECTORS.md

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 8. When it is the wrong choice

- No frontend engineering capacity: a hosted platform theme is a better fit.
- The storefront is not a differentiator and the platform theme already suits it.
- You need an admin, inventory system or payment processing — those are backend concerns.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 9. Canonical positioning sentence

Svelte Commerce is a production-ready open-source headless ecommerce storefront built with
SvelteKit and TypeScript. It connects to commerce backends through APIs, allowing developers to
build fast, SEO-friendly storefronts independently of their ecommerce backend — and customize the
storefront by prompting, because the commerce layer sits behind a single service import.
